scope: Narrow diagnostic after the user rejected the post-restart acceptance attempt. Neither diagnostic is acceptance, and no full regression or packaged sequence was started.

finding.currentDiagnostic: Electron enters the compiled application and acquires its isolated single-instance lock, but does not emit ready within 60000ms. Two instrumented-process snapshots and the uninstrumented probe show the main thread waiting on RPC endpoint \RPC Control\nlaplg, with target PID 2160. Independent tasklist /svc evidence identifies netprofm as the only service listed for that PID.
finding.attributionLimit: This establishes the live pre-ready RPC wait in the new probes. It does not retrospectively prove the cause of the earlier M1 timeout, explain why netprofm is not servicing the call, or establish a product, database or acceptance-harness defect.
finding.nextGate: Normal startup and complete clean shutdown/reopen must be demonstrated after environment recovery. A fresh complete schema-3 development sequence from M1 remains required before any packaged acceptance.

stages.detail: Direct electron.exe spawn; the sole argument is the diagnostic entry wrapper. No Chromium/Electron switches or NODE_OPTIONS. The wrapper loads unchanged out/main/index.js.
Original method return true. A unique isolated desktop-profile path avoids touching the planner workspace.
No ready event; ready=false when compiled entry returns. The external timer observes failure without altering Electron lifecycle.
better-sqlite3 module loading is observed, but its database constructor is never called. Ordo openRepository is inside app.whenReady().then.
No database constructor or pragma/exec calls. Opening the copied failed workspace did not reach repository initialization; no restore was requested in the narrow probe.
The source starts SymbolRenderHost lazily on a render request. No window, IPC registration or request was reached.
No browser-window-created event. Native snapshots contain only an untitled internal Chrome_WidgetWin_0, a power-message window and IME window; none is Ordo BrowserWindow readiness.
No web-contents-created or renderer load events.
No web contents or Ordo IPC handler registrations. No preload error or dialog was observed.
No renderer was created; no shell-ready claim.
No dialog calls in the logging wrapper and no modal dialog windows in native enumeration.

Uninstrumented PID 13080 / thread 8356 and instrumented PID 16492 / thread 10224 wait on \RPC Control\nlaplg to PID 2160. Instrumented native snapshots at 08:20:08.586Z and 08:20:43.528Z retain the same RPC chain. netprofm identity is separately retained.

shutdownAndReopen.earlierM1Run: The earlier failed manifest did not retain the first Electron process tree, quit-event timestamp, or descendant-exit timestamps. These cannot be reconstructed as a confirmed clean exit. Playwright uses shell:true on Windows, so its logged launched PID is not by itself proof of the entire Electron tree state.
shutdownAndReopen.beforeNewProbes: A read-only process enumeration before the new probes found no electron process. This is a current observation, not retrospective evidence of the earlier close/reopen boundary.

uninstrumentedProbe.observationCorrection: The first native observer incorrectly treated an untitled internal Chrome_WidgetWin_0 as a candidate window and posted WM_CLOSE to it. It did not observe a real Ordo window, clean exit, or shell readiness. That probe is not valid lifecycle success evidence; its live wait chain is retained. The scratch observer now requires the exact Ordo title before posting WM_CLOSE.

shutdownAndReopen.finalInventoryLimit: Both diagnostic PIDs were absent by the later inventory. No child-exit event or application quit event was retained after the bounded diagnostic controllers ended; disappearance is not accepted as a clean shutdown. No manual force-kill command was issued.
shutdownAndReopen.requirementStillPending: A successful normal shutdown with timestamped root/descendant exit confirmation followed by normal reopen remains unfulfilled because normal initial startup is blocked.

instrumentation.method: A separate scratch entry wrapper attaches event/log observers, records original lock/database/IPC/dialog calls and requires the current compiled main entry. The direct uninstrumented probe independently records the same RPC target.
instrumentation.removal: The active .test-data/m6-startup-observer.cjs entry was moved to startup-observer-source.cjs.txt in the evidence folder after both probes were absent. Product source/out never contained this logging. Acceptance paths do not reference the wrapper.

serviceRecovery.actionProposed: Normal administrator-level restart of netprofm only, with no forced stop or dependent/unrelated service action. No control has been sent.
